1	export type Tier = "free" | "pro";
2	
3	/** The three things that spend a model request. See docs/MONETISATION.md §2. */
4	export type GenerationKind = "drop" | "regenerate" | "styled";
5	
6	export type Entitlements = {
7	  tier: Tier;
8	  /**
9	   * Rerolls per DAY, across all occasions. null = unlimited.
10	   *
11	   * Global rather than per-occasion (user decision, 2026-08-05). Most people
12	   * care about one occasion on a given day, so a per-occasion allowance is
13	   * strictest exactly where attention goes and generous where nobody is
14	   * looking: you could be refused a second Work reroll while holding an unused
15	   * Evening one you never wanted.
16	   *
17	   * The usual objection to a global pool — that it can block an occasion you
18	   * have not opened yet — does not apply here, because a drop is free on every
19	   * tier. Tapping a new occasion is always a drop, so the pool only ever meters
20	   * rerolls.
21	   */
22	  regeneratesPerDay: number | null;
23	  /**
24	   * How many pieces a closet may hold. null = unlimited.
25	   *
26	   * Counts UNARCHIVED items only. Archiving is the user's way to make room —
27	   * there is no delete path in the product, so counting archived pieces would
28	   * strand a user at the cap with no way out. It also matches what the number
29	   * claims: an archived piece is not in your closet.
30	   *
31	   * 50 is deliberately well clear of the ~20-30 range where combo coverage
32	   * thins (PR #15 measured a 21-item closet at 21 combos in winter against 48
33	   * in summer), so the free tier never experiences a starved stylist — it
34	   * experiences a full one, with a ceiling.
35	   */
36	  closetItems: number | null;
37	  /** "Style an outfit with this" — Pro #2. */
38	  styledLooks: boolean;
39	  savedOutfits: number | null;
40	  /** The Wear Stats SCREEN. The per-item tile on item detail is free. */
41	  analytics: boolean;
42	  gapAnalysis: boolean;
43	  packingMode: boolean;
44	};
45	
46	/**
47	 * The tiers, as data. See docs/MONETISATION.md for the reasoning — in short:
48	 * meter what costs us money, sell what compounds, and never gate the daily
49	 * drop, the share card, or the closet.
50	 *
51	 * The free ceiling is four occasion drops plus three rerolls = 7 generations a
52	 * day, about $0.63/month at $0.003 each and nearer $0.20 in realistic use.
53	 * **The ceiling is the point** — a free tier needs a worst case you can
54	 * survive, and this one cannot be raised by adding clothes.
55	 */
56	export const FREE: Entitlements = {
57	  tier: "free",
58	  regeneratesPerDay: 3,
59	  closetItems: 50,
60	  styledLooks: false,
61	  savedOutfits: 10,
62	  analytics: false,
63	  gapAnalysis: false,
64	  packingMode: false,
65	};
66	
67	export const PRO: Entitlements = {
68	  tier: "pro",
69	  regeneratesPerDay: null,
70	  closetItems: null,
71	  styledLooks: true,
72	  savedOutfits: null,
73	  analytics: true,
74	  gapAnalysis: true,
75	  packingMode: true,
76	};
77	
78	// The pure functions live HERE, not in entitlements.ts, so tests can import them
79	// without dragging in `server-only` (which does not resolve under jsdom).
80	// entitlements.ts re-exports them for app code.
81	
82	/** Unknown input resolves to free: capabilities fail CLOSED. */
83	export function entitlementsFor(tier: unknown): Entitlements {
84	  return tier === "pro" ? PRO : FREE;
85	}
86	
87	export type GenerationCheck = {
88	  allowed: boolean;
89	  /** null = unlimited. Only meaningful for a metered kind. */
90	  remaining: number | null;
91	  reason?: string;
92	};
93	
94	/**
95	 * May this user spend a model request right now?
96	 *
97	 * `regeneratesUsed` is the user's total reroll count for their local today,
98	 * across every occasion.
99	 *
100	 * A drop is never metered on any tier: MONETISATION §1 and Decision 4 both say
101	 * the daily drop is the product, and rationing it is how nobody discovers the
102	 * magic. That is also what makes a global reroll pool safe — a user can always
103	 * open any occasion, so the pool can never strand them.
104	 */
105	export function checkGeneration(
106	  e: Entitlements,
107	  input: { kind: GenerationKind; regeneratesUsed: number },
108	): GenerationCheck {
109	  if (input.kind === "drop") return { allowed: true, remaining: null };
110	
111	  if (input.kind === "styled") {
112	    return e.styledLooks
113	      ? { allowed: true, remaining: null }
114	      : {
115	          allowed: false,
116	          remaining: 0,
117	          reason: "Building a look around a piece is a Pro feature.",
118	        };
119	  }
120	
121	  if (e.regeneratesPerDay == null) return { allowed: true, remaining: null };
122	  const remaining = Math.max(0, e.regeneratesPerDay - input.regeneratesUsed);
123	  return remaining > 0
124	    ? { allowed: true, remaining }
125	    : {
126	        allowed: false,
127	        remaining: 0,
128	        reason: `That's your ${e.regeneratesPerDay} rerolls for today. Pro rerolls without limit.`,
129	      };
130	}
131	
132	/**
133	 * May this user add another piece?
134	 *
135	 * `held` is the number of UNARCHIVED pieces already in the closet — archiving
136	 * is how a free user makes room, since nothing in the product deletes an item.
137	 */
138	export function checkCloset(e: Entitlements, held: number): GenerationCheck {
139	  if (e.closetItems == null) return { allowed: true, remaining: null };
140	  const remaining = Math.max(0, e.closetItems - held);
141	  return remaining > 0
142	    ? { allowed: true, remaining }
143	    : {
144	        allowed: false,
145	        remaining: 0,
146	        reason: `A free closet holds ${e.closetItems} pieces. Pro is unlimited — or archive something you no longer wear.`,
147	      };
148	}

content.text:
I've reviewed all changed and referenced files. Analysis:

1. **`items` count query (line 45)** omits an explicit `.eq("user_id", user.id)` filter, but `supabase/migrations/20260615114702_items.sql` enables RLS with policy `items_all_own` restricting to `auth.uid() = user_id`. The server client uses the anon key + user session cookies, so RLS scopes the count. Not exploitable.

2. **`wear_logs` query (line 46)** has an explicit `user_id` filter AND is protected by `wear_logs_own` RLS policy. Safe.

3. **`handleFrom(user.email)` / `initials(...)`**: displays the user's *own* email components back to themselves — no cross-user exposure, no sink.

4. **`localDateFor(new Date(), profile?.location_timezone ?? "UTC")`**: `Intl.DateTimeFormat` throws are caught, falls back to UTC. Timezone string only reaches `Intl.DateTimeFormat`'s validator — no path/eval/shell sink.

5. **`entitlementsFor(profile?.tier)`**: correctly fails closed to `FREE` for any non-`"pro"` value. The `tier` displayed here is read-only presentation.

6. **`currentStreak(wornDates, today)`**: pure computation over date strings (DB type `date`, always well-formed). No sinks.

7. **Sign-out form**: standard POST to `/auth/signout`, unchanged in intent from prior code.

8. **`LINKS` const**: static hrefs, not user-controlled; rendered via `next/link`. `ProfileHub` renders `link.href`/`label`/`desc` as text with default React escaping. No XSS.

9. **`ProfileHub` presentational component**: renders `name`, `handle`, `initials`, `archetype` via React text nodes (auto-escaped); `palette` values are hex-token literals from a static `DNA` map, not user input, so inlining into `style={{background: c}}` is safe.

No source→sink path with an attacker-controlled value and no mitigation. Returning empty findings.
